Senses.PreferredTarget: meet a buddha, kill the buddha
AlternateTargets: on meeting a buddha, kill the buddha
when you meet a buddha, kill the buddha
encountering a buddha, kill the buddha
Senses.Explanation: The four graphs mean “meet,” “buddha,” “kill,” and “buddha”: “meet a buddha, kill the buddha.” In Linji's recorded address to followers, it is the first member of a longer series: do not be deluded by others; whatever is met inside or outside is to be killed on contact—buddha, patriarch, arhat, father and mother, and kin—only then obtaining release. Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters preserves the same passage without punctuation. A later lamp record explicitly attributes the saying to Linji and then asks why someone called a good teacher would want to kill people and what principle this is; the question is left standing. In the Five Lamps Compendium, Jingyin Kumu Facheng uses the shorter pair “meet a buddha, kill the buddha; meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch,” followed by “heaven cannot contain him; hell has no gate to gather him.” These records provide the wording, its surrounding series, later questions about it, and later deployments; this entry does not supply an interpretation they do not state.
Senses.Note: Linji's full series supplies the earliest frame represented here. The headword alone occurs 60 times across 50 allowlisted texts, while the extended pair with “meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch” also circulates. Later records both quote the saying under Linji's name and place its short form inside other masters' addresses. Compare “meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch” and “kill buddhas and patriarchs.”

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji's own record: an address to followers. The excerpt preserves the frame and first member of the complete five-part killing series, which closes with “only then obtaining release.”

Senses.PreferredTarget: meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch
AlternateTargets: on meeting a patriarch, kill the patriarch
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch" (逢祖殺祖). Linji's surviving record places it inside a five-member roster: "meet buddha, kill buddha; meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch; meet an arhat, kill the arhat; meet parents, kill parents; meet kin, kill kin" (逢佛殺佛、逢祖殺祖、逢羅漢殺羅漢、逢父母殺父母、逢親眷殺親眷). This is the Chan bend: the honored religious and familial titles become the grammatical objects of the same repeated verb, and later masters preserve, question, and redeploy that severe roster. A successor record explicitly asks why a good teacher would want to kill people after quoting the three religious members, without supplying a prose gloss. Later uses attach the phrase to a sharp sword, place it opposite "carry the infant and encourage the child" (提攜赤子，撫獎嬰兒) in a contrast about grandmotherly kindness, or quote it in a New Year's address before comments on lineage descent. The records use killing language literally in the formula but do not record bodily killings in these deployments; this entry adds no symbolic object behind the named roster.
Senses.Note: The exact shorter string has 57 hits in 47 allowlisted texts. It is almost always paired with 'meet buddha, kill buddha' and often extended with 'meet an arhat, kill the arhat.' Linji's fuller roster is primary; later uses include quotation, interrogation, sword language, verse, and explicit contrast with grandmotherly care.

Occurrences.Kwic: 向裏向外逢著便殺——逢佛殺佛、逢祖殺祖、逢羅漢殺羅漢、逢父母殺父母、逢親眷殺親眷——始得解脫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji's record supplies the fullest roster, extending the repeated verb from buddha and patriarch through arhat, parents, and kin.

Occurrences.Kwic: 逢佛殺佛逢祖殺祖逢羅漢殺羅漢。既稱善知識。為什麼却要殺人去。且道是什麼道理。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A Continued Lamp record quotes Linji's three religious objects and explicitly asks why a good teacher would want to kill people.

Occurrences.Kwic: 逢佛殺佛、逢祖殺祖、逢羅漢殺羅漢。真淨老人自謂臨濟正傳黃龍的子，七出八沒，得大自由。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A New Year's address quotes the three-part roster immediately before examining a claim to Linji succession through Huanglong.

Occurrences.Kwic: 或問：『為何二十五年前無老婆心？』但云：『逢佛殺佛，逢祖殺祖。』『二十五年後為何有老婆心？』但云：『提攜赤子，撫獎嬰兒。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baiyu places the phrase as the answer for lacking grandmotherly kindness, opposite carrying an infant and encouraging a child.

Occurrences.Kwic: 單提一把吹毛利劒。逢佛殺佛逢祖殺祖。直教一物不得當其前。一法莫能隨其後。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng's address places the paired formula after taking up a hair-blowing sharp sword and before allowing no thing or formulation ahead of it.
